evidence: All five dimension prompts and every criterion describe HireOps only; no residue found. (1) Template residue: none of the template's CHANGE_ME placeholders remain; app_context.md names HireOps at http://localhost:3000; test.sh:198-200 substitutes {app_context} into every */*/prompt.md. A case-insensitive grep of tests/ and instruction.md for sibling/generic nouns (colderwater, ledger, invoice, warehouse, clinic, patient, tenant, ticket, lorem, example.com, admin@, demo, TODO, placeholder) returned nothing. (2) Credentials: app_context.md lists the same 10 accounts, roles and password Hireops!2026 as instruction.md and seed users (USR-REC1..3 recruiters, USR-MGR1..3 hiring_manager, USR-OBS1 observer, USR-CAN1..3 candidates). Every name used in prompts/criteria (Rafael Costa, Mei Lin, Ingrid Sorensen, Bill Okafor, Aud Halvorsen, Noor Haddad, Tomas Varga, Lena Fischer) is a seeded account in the stated role. (3) Screens/entities: Board with stages Applied/Screen/Interview/Offer/Hired/Rejected, Conversations, Activity and candidate applications view match instruction.md and hireops_rules.md section 3/4/7; candidate wording in hro_candidate_view matches seed candidate_status_labels exactly; page size 30 in hro_thread_latest/earlier matches seed thread_page_size 30 and rules section 6; 401/403/404 statuses in hro_anonymous and hro_candidate_private match rules section 1. (4) Seed facts quoted in prompts were re-derived from seed_data.json: Platform Engineer Applied = Greta Lindqvist(1), Ade Bello(2), Marco Rossi(3); Screen = Priya Nair(1), Samuel Ortiz(2) (functional prompt.md:25, hro_restart); Noor's APP-101 note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' matches; Noor PE conversation has 120 messages (app_context.md); Lena (USR-CAN3) read_count 2 of 3 messages on APP-301 Product Designer, last by USR-REC3 -> 1 unread (functional Z, hro_unread_counts); Tomas's seeded Data Analyst conversation APP-201 exists for the T fallback, and its job JOB-DATA is managed by Bill (USR-MGR2), so Bill/Ingrid access expectations in hro_thread_access remain correct under the fallback; rules example 'Mei Lin moved Priya Nair from Screen to Interview' uses real seeded names. (5) Internal consistency of the scripted functional protocols was traced by hand: M (A lands below B after B,A ordering), L (Interview 2/2 -> A to Offer, E in, E out, Mei moves A back -> undo of E would make 3 > 2, refused), B (V undo returns V to top; Y up two gives Y,W,X,Z,A2; bulk W,X,Y arrives Y,W,X below V; V+Z skip refused; V,W,X 3>2 refused; A2+V arrive A2,V by board order) all agree with hireops_rules.md section 3. Every cross-referenced criterion id (hro_activity_refusals, hro_candidate_linked, hro_restart, hro_bulk_move, hro_bulk_places, hro_undo_full, hro_msg_compose, hro_msg_exchange, hro_candidate_private) exists in functional/judge.toml; restart_app matches tools/restart_mcp.py:14 and judge.toml wires $APP_RESTART_HELPER exported at test.sh:193. (6) Deliverable: every prompt targets http://localhost:3000 and the Node/Express/SQLite app described in instruction.md; visual prompt scope (desktop, no phone/theme) matches instruction.md. Counterexample attempts: a conforming app could fail only if a prompt asserted a wrong seed fact, role, account or stage name; none was found. A broken app cannot benefit from a misdescription since none exists. Minor non-defect note: the in-dimension global gate text in scored/functional:11, polish:11 and visual:11 lists title, hiring manager and places but omits team and candidate source, while gates/constraints criterion and rules section 2 include them; a judge supplies required fields through the UI, so this is wording drift, not an inaccurate description of the app. This row is a source-level review; no judge run was needed or claimed, and this is not evidence of any Oracle, model or portal score.
